evidence.title: Book bans reach all-time high, led by Texas and Florida and fueled by AI

occurrences.checkable_against: Texas Freedom to Read Project public-records request and AI book-vetting records
occurrences.quote_span: In some cases, AI recommended removing a book because another district had removed it and not because it actually included obscene material.
occurrences.speaker: outlet's own
occurrences.subject: PEN America book bans report

occurrences.checkable_against: AI book-scanning outputs and the full text/context of flagged books
occurrences.quote_span: AI sometimes pulls up certain phrases in a book that could be “troublesome” based on state law without “looking at what is the context of those words in the book,” leading to false conclusions about its appropriateness for schools, he added.
occurrences.speaker: Skip Dye
occurrences.subject: PEN America book bans report

occurrences.checkable_against: PEN America book-ban count methodology and public-records requests
occurrences.quote_span: “The fact that a huge number, a strong majority, I would say, of the bans that we calculated in Texas and Florida — we were only able to find out about because of public information requests,” said Philomena Polefrone, senior manager for Freedom to Read at PEN America, adding it has become difficult to count book bans based on local reporting.
occurrences.speaker: Philomena Polefrone
occurrences.subject: PEN America book bans report

occurrences.checkable_against: PEN America book bans report for 2025-2026
occurrences.quote_span: Book bans reached an all-time high this year as political pressure and AI fuel a spike in titles taken off the shelves.
occurrences.speaker: outlet's own
occurrences.subject: PEN America book bans report

occurrences.checkable_against: PEN America book-bans report methodology and source records
occurrences.quote_span: “This is the first time that we have direct evidence of” AI use in our report, Polefrone said.
occurrences.speaker: Philomena Polefrone
occurrences.subject: PEN America book bans report

occurrences.checkable_against: PEN America 2025-2026 book bans report
occurrences.quote_span: Almost 12,000 books were banned between 2025 and 2026, a 5,000-book jump from the previous year, according to a Monday report by PEN America, a free-speech organization.
occurrences.speaker: PEN America
occurrences.subject: PEN America book bans report

occurrences.checkable_against: PEN America 2025-2026 book bans report
occurrences.quote_span: The vast majority of the book bans are coming out of Texas and Florida, with an estimated 8,100 and 3,200 titles revoked, respectively.
occurrences.speaker: PEN America
occurrences.subject: PEN America book bans report

occurrences.checkable_against: School-board and educator AI book-scanning records
occurrences.quote_span: “I do know that some school boards and some educators have been using AI tools to go through and scan books to go and look for possible books” that could violate state law, Dye said.
occurrences.speaker: Skip Dye
occurrences.subject: PEN America book bans report

occurrences.checkable_against: PEN America 2025-2026 book bans report
occurrences.quote_span: Almost 12,000 books were banned between 2025 and 2026, a 5,000-book jump from the previous year, according to a Monday report by PEN America, a free-speech organization.
occurrences.speaker: PEN America
occurrences.subject: PEN America book bans report

occurrences.checkable_against: PEN America book-bans report methodology and state-level source data
occurrences.quote_span: In a distant third to Texas and Florida is Ohio with 117 bans, though PEN America believes the numbers point to an undercount in most states.
occurrences.speaker: PEN America
occurrences.subject: PEN America book bans report

occurrences.checkable_against: PEN America 2025-2026 book bans report
occurrences.quote_span: The vast majority of the book bans are coming out of Texas and Florida, with an estimated 8,100 and 3,200 titles revoked, respectively.
occurrences.speaker: PEN America
occurrences.subject: PEN America book bans report

occurrences.checkable_against: PEN America book-ban report methodology and state-level source data
occurrences.quote_span: “We have needed to pivot a little bit and start going directly to the source for information. And so, I would also say that the fact that Texas and Florida are very overrepresented in our report this year doesn’t indicate that there aren’t bans in other states. It indicates that we have better information in Texas and Florida,” Polefrone added.
occurrences.speaker: Philomena Polefrone
occurrences.subject: PEN America book bans report

occurrences.checkable_against: Penguin Random House Intellectual Freedom Task Force statements and school book-review records
occurrences.quote_span: The group has also noticed the rise of AI as educators navigate laws around which books are allowed in classrooms, highlighting how the technology could incorrectly flag books for removal.
occurrences.speaker: Penguin Random House Intellectual Freedom Task Force
occurrences.subject: PEN America book bans report

occurrences.checkable_against: Texas Freedom to Read Project public-records request and responsive school records
occurrences.quote_span: Through a public records request, the Texas Freedom to Read Project found multiple schools using AI to vet books.
occurrences.speaker: Texas Freedom to Read Project
occurrences.subject: PEN America book bans report

occurrences.checkable_against: Penguin Random House survey of New York educators and school-library acquisition records
occurrences.quote_span: “We’ve also seen even some blue states … like even New York itself here, where we’ve actually seen and surveyed New York educators and found that they, too, feel nervous about books, and they have preemptively been making choices: either removing books that they have on their shelves because they’re afraid a parent could complain” or avoiding buying certain titles altogether, said Skip Dye, senior vice president at Penguin Random House and chair of the group’s Intellectual Freedom Task Force.
occurrences.speaker: Skip Dye
occurrences.subject: PEN America book bans report
